claims.statement: Since 28 June 2025, covered cultural goods imported from outside the EU require, depending on type, an import-licence application, importer statement, or standardised description through the electronic ICG module in TRACES NT.

A person importing archaeological objects or parts of monuments older than 250 years from a third country must apply for an import licence in the member state where the goods first enter a qualifying customs procedure.
Licence applications, electronic signatures, importer statements, and transmission to customs are handled through ICG, making the dossier a concrete digital border gate.

contrary_evidence: ICG is already the public authoritative system, and specialist customs agents or lawyers may bundle dossier preparation.
Covered cultural-goods import volume may be too small in Poland alone, making EU-wide channel expansion essential.

economics.acquisition_route: Pilot with one Polish art-logistics or customs firm and one auction house, process 20 historical/sandbox dossiers, then offer a white-label intake portal to EU specialist shippers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 250 EU trade firms at 24000 PLN ARR plus 2500 dossiers at 1600 PLN yields 10m PLN revenue; at 22% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 70% founder ownership, equity could exceed 6.1m PLN in years 6-9. Validate the niche's transaction count and exclude retained cash from a second count.
economics.founder_time: 2.5-4 hours per day for workflow and evidence tooling; contract cultural-property and customs experts per case and never make unsupervised legal determinations
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 58-75% while experts review cases, rising above 80% for repeat counterparties and standard importer statements
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 9-15 months at 18 monthly dossiers averaging 1800 PLN plus five firm subscriptions; validate case mix and expert-review cost
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 900-3500 PLN per standard object dossier, 5000-15000 PLN for complex licence cases, and 6000-24000 PLN annual vault subscriptions for trade firms
economics.retention_or_repeat: Provenance evidence is reused for insurance, resale, finance, export, and future import; trusted custody and version history create long-lived switching cost

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned object-document-owner-jurisdiction graph with prior authority outcomes detects gaps, prevents evidence loss, and becomes valuable again at resale, insurance, financing, or re-import
fingerprint.customer: EU auction houses, antiquities and art dealers, museums, specialist art shippers, and customs representatives importing cultural goods from outside the EU
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label through art-logistics firms, auction software, specialist insurers, conservators, customs representatives, and trade associations that repeatedly handle objects
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Object classification intake, provenance evidence escrow, standard description, ICG licence or statement packet, authority workflow tracking, and reusable resale/insurance dossier
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The dealer, auction house, or customs representative pays per object dossier when accepting the consignment and annually for provenance-vault custody
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A third-country acquisition or consignment may enter the EU only after its category, age, provenance, description, and required ICG document are resolved

founder_fit: Strong fit with forensic data lineage, anomaly detection, and document automation
Concentrated B2B intermediaries offer low-volume, high-value distribution without a personal media brand
Can validate with historical or test dossiers under the 5-hour daily constraint
Low capital intensity, provided legal and cultural-property judgement is delegated
risks: Provenance evidence may be forged, incomplete, disputed, or legally sensitive.
A classification or licence error can delay valuable objects and expose the service to claims.
The niche may demand reputation and domain relationships that take years to build.

structure.control_point: the ICG import licence or importer statement transmitted to customs before covered cultural goods enter the EU
structure.critical_dependency: trusted handling of sensitive provenance documents and expert determination of object category, age, origin, and documentary sufficiency

thesis: Build a provenance-evidence escrow and ICG dossier service for EU auction houses, antiquities dealers, museums, specialist customs agents, and art-logistics firms importing cultural goods from third countries. Before purchase or consignment acceptance, the service identifies the object category and age, collects ownership/export history and standardised descriptions, hashes and versions supporting evidence, and prepares the correct ICG import-licence application or importer statement for electronic delivery to customs. Distribution is concentrated through auction-management software, specialist shippers, insurers, conservators, and customs agents rather than individual collectors. A privacy-preserving object-to-owner-to-document-to-authority-outcome graph can become the trusted provenance rail for repeat trade, insurance, finance, resale, and lawful border movement across the EU.
title: CultureGate ICG Provenance Escrow
uncertainties: Annual covered-object volume and current dossier fees across EU specialist firms
Whether auction houses and insurers will trust an early-stage digital escrow
Delegated ICG access, qualified-signature workflow, and professional-liability requirements
